sehemu: Part III: The Prime Minister, the Cabinet and the Government
maudhui: (1) There shall be a Director of Public Prosecutions who shall be appointed by the President from among persons possessing the qualifications specified in Article 59(2) and who have continuously held such qualifications for a period of not less than ten years. (2) The Director of Public Prosecutions shall have power to institute, conduct and supervise all criminal prosecutions in the country. (3) The powers of the Director of Public Prosecutions under subarticle (2) may be exercised by him personally or on his instructions by officers under him, or by other persons performing those functions on his instructions. (4) In exercising his powers, the Director of Public Prosecutions shall be independent and shall not be subject to the direction or control of any person or authority, and shall have regard to the following matters: (a) the need to do justice; (b) the prevention of abuse of the legal process; and (c) the public interest. (5) The Director of Public Prosecutions shall exercise his powers as prescribed by any law enacted or to be enacted by Parliament.
